audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel / Shemuel Aleph chapter 25, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Samuel's burial, Carmel shearing economy, protection/payment claim, Nabal's class contempt, David's planned collective killing, Abigail's provision and intervention, bloodguilt language, Nabal's collapse, immediate marriage proposal, plural marriage, and Michal's transfer.

verses.restored: Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. David arose and went down to wilderness of Paran.

familiar.text: And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

modern.text: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David set out and went down to the Wilderness of Paran. David, Nabal, and Abigail

original.text: וַיָּ֣מָת שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּקָּבְצ֤וּ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּסְפְּדוּ ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖רֶד אֶל מִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן

verses.restored: There was a man in Maon whose work was in Carmel. The man was very great: he had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

familiar.text: And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

modern.text: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.

original.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ בְּמָע֜וֹן וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ בַכַּרְמֶ֗ל וְהָאִישׁ֙ גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֔ד וְל֛וֹ צֹ֥אן שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאֶ֣לֶף עִזִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֛י בִּגְזֹ֥ז אֶת צֹאנ֖וֹ בַּכַּרְמֶֽל

verses.restored: Name of the man was Nabal, and name of his wife was Abigail. The woman was of good understanding and beautiful in form, but the man was harsh and evil in his deeds; he was a Calebite.

familiar.text: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.

modern.text: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.

original.text: וְשֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ נָבָ֔ל וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֲבִגָ֑יִל וְהָאִשָּׁ֤ה טֽוֹבַת שֶׂ֨כֶל֙ וִ֣יפַת תֹּ֔אַר וְהָאִ֥ישׁ קָשֶׁ֛ה וְרַ֥ע מַעֲלָלִ֖ים וְה֥וּא כלבו

verses.restored: David heard in wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

familiar.text: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal did shear his sheep.

modern.text: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי גֹזֵ֥ז נָבָ֖ל אֶת צֹאנֽוֹ

verses.restored: David sent ten young men. David said to young men, Go up to Carmel, come to Nabal, and ask him in my name concerning peace.

familiar.text: And David sent out ten young men, and David said unto the young men, Get you up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:

modern.text: So David sent ten young men and instructed them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel. Greet him in my name

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לַנְּעָרִ֗ים עֲל֤וּ כַרְמֶ֨לָה֙ וּבָאתֶ֣ם אֶל נָבָ֔ל וּשְׁאֶלְתֶּם ל֥וֹ בִשְׁמִ֖י לְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Thus you shall say: To life! Peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that is yours.

familiar.text: And thus shall ye say to him that liveth in prosperity, Peace be both to thee, and peace be to thine house, and peace be unto all that thou hast.

modern.text: and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and your house and to all that belongs to you.

original.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֥ם כֹּ֖ה לֶחָ֑י וְאַתָּ֤ה שָׁלוֹם֙ וּבֵיתְךָ֣ שָׁל֔וֹם וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us; we did not shame/harm them, and nothing of theirs was missing all days they were in Carmel.

familiar.text: And now I have heard that thou hast shearers: now thy shepherds which were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there ought missing unto them, all the while they were in Carmel.

modern.text: Now I hear that it is time for shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we did not harass them, and nothing of theirs was missing the whole time they were in Carmel.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י גֹזְזִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ עַתָּ֗ה הָרֹעִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֙ הָי֣וּ עִמָּ֔נוּ לֹ֣א הֶכְלַמְנ֗וּם וְלֹֽא נִפְקַ֤ד לָהֶם֙ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל יְמֵ֖י הֱיוֹתָ֥ם בַּכַּרְמֶֽל

verses.restored: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Let my young men find favor in your eyes, because we have come on a good/festive day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to David your son.

familiar.text: Ask thy young men, and they will shew thee. Wherefore let the young men find favour in thine eyes: for we come in a good day: give, I pray thee, whatsoever cometh to thine hand unto thy servants, and to thy son David.

modern.text: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor with you, for we have come on the day of a feast. Please give whatever you can afford to your servants and to your son David.’”

original.text: שְׁאַ֨ל אֶת נְעָרֶ֜יךָ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֗ךְ וְיִמְצְא֨וּ הַנְּעָרִ֥ים חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי עַל י֥וֹם ט֖וֹב בָּ֑נוּ תְּנָה נָּ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּלְבִנְךָ֖ לְדָוִֽד

verses.restored: David's young men came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in David's name, and they rested/waited.

familiar.text: And when David’s young men came, they spake to Nabal according to all those words in the name of David, and ceased.

modern.text: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ נַעֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַיְדַבְּר֧וּ אֶל נָבָ֛ל כְּכָל הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בְּשֵׁ֣ם דָּוִ֑ד וַיָּנֽוּחוּ

verses.restored: Nabal answered David's servants and said, Who is David, and who is son of Jesse? Today many servants are breaking away, each from before his master.

familiar.text: And Nabal answered David’s servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master.

modern.text: But Nabal asked them, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן נָבָ֜ל אֶת עַבְדֵ֤י דָוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י דָוִ֖ד וּמִ֣י בֶן יִשָׁ֑י הַיּוֹם֙ רַבּ֣וּ עֲבָדִ֔ים הַמִּתְפָּ֣רְצִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵ֥י אֲדֹנָֽיו

verses.restored: Shall I take my bread, my water, and my slaughtered meat that I slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men whom I do not know—from where they are?

familiar.text: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men, whom I know not whence they be?

modern.text: Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?”

original.text: וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶת לַחְמִי֙ וְאֶת מֵימַ֔י וְאֵת֙ טִבְחָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר טָבַ֖חְתִּי לְגֹֽזְזָ֑י וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ לַֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה הֵֽמָּה

verses.restored: David's young men turned to their way, returned, and came and told him according to all these words.

familiar.text: So David’s young men turned their way, and went again, and came and told him all those sayings.

modern.text: So David’s men turned around and went back, and they relayed to him all these words.

original.text: וַיַּהַפְכ֥וּ נַעֲרֵֽי דָוִ֖ד לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֔אוּ וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ כְּכֹ֖ל הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: David said to his men, Each man gird on his sword. Each man girded on his sword, and David also girded on his sword. About four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred stayed with baggage.

familiar.text: And David said unto his men, Gird ye on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the stuff.

modern.text: And David said to his men, “Strap on your swords!” So David and all his men put on their swords, and about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חִגְר֣וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת חַרְבּ֗וֹ וַֽיַּחְגְּרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת חַרְבּ֔וֹ וַיַּחְגֹּ֥ר גַּם דָּוִ֖ד אֶת חַרְבּ֑וֹ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד כְּאַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ אִ֔ישׁ וּמָאתַ֖יִם יָשְׁב֥וּ עַל הַכֵּלִֽים

verses.restored: One young man from the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, Look, David sent messengers from wilderness to bless/greet our master, and he screamed insults at them.

familiar.text: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.

modern.text: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he scolded them.

original.text: וְלַאֲבִיגַ֨יִל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת נָבָ֔ל הִגִּ֧יד נַֽעַר אֶחָ֛ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד מַלְאָכִ֧ים מֵֽהַמִּדְבָּ֛ר לְבָרֵ֥ךְ אֶת אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וַיָּ֥עַט בָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: Yet the men were very good to us. We were not shamed/harmed, and we missed nothing all days we walked with them while we were in field.

familiar.text: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:

modern.text: Yet these men were very good to us. When we were in the field, we were not harassed, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we lived among them.

original.text: וְהָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים טֹבִ֥ים לָ֖נוּ מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֤א הָכְלַ֨מְנוּ֙ וְלֹֽא פָקַ֣דְנוּ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל יְמֵי֙ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ אִתָּ֔ם בִּֽהְיוֹתֵ֖נוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: They were a wall around us both night and day, all days we were with them shepherding flock.

familiar.text: They were a wall unto us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.

modern.text: They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.

original.text: חוֹמָה֙ הָי֣וּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ גַּם לַ֖יְלָה גַּם יוֹמָ֑ם כָּל יְמֵ֛י הֱיוֹתֵ֥נוּ עִמָּ֖ם רֹעִ֥ים הַצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: Now know and see what you should do, because evil is determined against our master and against all his house. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him.

familiar.text: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a son of Belial, that a man cannot speak to him.

modern.text: Now consider carefully what you must do, because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!” Abigail Intercedes for Nabal

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה דְּעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ מַֽה תַּעֲשִׂ֔י כִּֽי כָלְתָ֧ה הָרָעָ֛ה אֶל אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וְעַ֣ל כָּל בֵּית֑וֹ וְהוּא֙ בֶּן בְּלִיַּ֔עַל מִדַּבֵּ֖ר אֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep prepared, five seahs of roasted grain, one hundred clusters/cakes of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and placed them upon donkeys.

familiar.text: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.

modern.text: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys

original.text: וַתְּמַהֵ֣ר אבוגיל וַתִּקַּח֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּשְׁנַ֣יִם נִבְלֵי יַ֗יִן וְחָמֵ֨שׁ צֹ֤אן עשוות וְחָמֵ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קָלִ֔י וּמֵאָ֥ה צִמֻּקִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם דְּבֵלִ֑ים וַתָּ֖שֶׂם עַל הַחֲמֹרִֽים

verses.restored: She said to her young men, Pass before me; look, I am coming after you. But she did not tell Nabal her husband.

familiar.text: And she said unto her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.

modern.text: and said to her young men, “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לִנְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י הִנְנִ֖י אַחֲרֵיכֶ֣ם בָּאָ֑ה וּלְאִישָׁ֥הּ נָבָ֖ל לֹ֥א הִגִּֽידָה

verses.restored: As she was riding upon donkey and descending in concealment of mountain, look, David and his men were descending toward her, and she met them.

familiar.text: And it was so, as she rode on the ass, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down against her; and she met them.

modern.text: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.

original.text: וְהָיָ֞ה הִ֣יא רֹכֶ֣בֶת עַֽל הַחֲמ֗וֹר וְיֹרֶ֨דֶת֙ בְּסֵ֣תֶר הָהָ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה דָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו יֹרְדִ֖ים לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַתִּפְגֹּ֖שׁ אֹתָֽם

verses.restored: David had said, Surely for emptiness I guarded all that belongs to this man in wilderness, so that nothing was missing from all that belonged to him; yet he returned to me evil in place of good.

familiar.text: Now David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow hath in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained unto him: and he hath requited me evil for good.

modern.text: Now David had just finished saying, “In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness. Nothing that belongs to him has gone missing, yet he has paid me back evil for good.

original.text: וְדָוִ֣ד אָמַ֗ר אַךְ֩ לַשֶּׁ֨קֶר שָׁמַ֜רְתִּי אֶֽת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָזֶה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְלֹא נִפְקַ֥ד מִכָּל אֲשֶׁר ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָה וַיָּֽשֶׁב לִ֥י רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה

verses.restored: Thus may Divine do to enemies of David, and thus add, if I leave from all that belongs to him until morning even one male—literally, one who urinates against wall.

familiar.text: So and more also do God unto the enemies of David, if I leave of all that pertain to him by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.

modern.text: May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one of Nabal’s men survive until morning.”

original.text: כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֑יף אִם אַשְׁאִ֧יר מִכָּל אֲשֶׁר ל֛וֹ עַד הַבֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּקִֽיר

verses.restored: Abigail saw David, hurried and descended from donkey, fell before David upon her face, and bowed to ground.

familiar.text: And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,

modern.text: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.

original.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֲבִיגַ֨יִל֙ אֶת דָּוִ֔ד וַתְּמַהֵ֕ר וַתֵּ֖רֶד מֵעַ֣ל הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַתִּפֹּ֞ל לְאַפֵּ֤י דָוִד֙ עַל פָּנֶ֔יהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: She fell at his feet and said, On me, my lord, let this guilt be on me. Please let your maidservant speak in your ears, and hear words of your maidservant.

familiar.text: And fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: and let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine audience, and hear the words of thine handmaid.

modern.text: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.

translation_notes: Abigail is the chapter's principal moral agent: she gathers intelligence, distributes resources, confronts an armed leader, names bloodguilt, and stops a household massacre.
David's protection of Nabal's shepherds may create a real social claim to generosity, but refusal of payment does not justify extortion, retaliation, or collective punishment.
The idiom 'one who urinates against wall' is a contemptuous male-targeting expression. It should not be sanitized into a heroic oath or used as gender policing.
Abigail's statement 'on me be the guilt' is strategic intercession, not confession that she caused Nabal's insult or David's planned violence.
David explicitly admits that he intended to kill every male in the household. His later kingship does not excuse the plan.
Nabal's bodily collapse and death may not be used to claim that illness, stroke, cardiac crisis, or sudden death proves Divine punishment.

David's marriage proposal arrives immediately after Nabal's death through his servants and amid a large power imbalance. Abigail's gestures and servant language do not establish modern standards of free consent.
Michal's transfer to Palti exposes royal control over women's relationships. Neither Saul nor David owns her, and she may not be treated as a dynastic object.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not romanticize David's attempted extortion or planned household massacre. Do not blame Abigail for male violence, preach strategic submission as every survivor's duty, or treat her marriage as proof that intervention earns romantic reward.
